title: Gold plated silver jewellery: is it worth it?
description: Gold plated silver gives you a gold look on a real 925 silver base. Here is what you get, how long the plating lasts, and who it suits best before you buy.
keywords: is gold plated silver worth it
how long does gold plating last on silver
intro: Gold plated silver is worth it if you want the warm look of gold for everyday wear without paying for solid gold, and you are fine with the plating needing care or a re-plate someday. Its big advantage over gold plated brass is what remains underneath: real 925 silver, not a base metal that discolours.

sections.heading: What you are actually buying
paragraphs: A gold plated silver piece starts as sterling silver, 92.5% silver. A thin layer of gold is then bonded to the surface, usually through electroplating. The finished piece looks yellow or rose gold, but its weight, strength and most of its value come from the silver.

You may also see the word vermeil. It is generally used for gold over sterling silver with a thicker gold layer than ordinary flash plating, though how strictly the term is used varies between sellers and countries. If a listing says vermeil, it is fair to ask how thick the gold layer is.

sections.heading: The honest pros and cons
paragraphs: It helps to see both sides together before deciding.
list: Pro: the look of gold at a fraction of the price of solid gold jewellery.
Pro: a real precious-metal base, so it does not turn green or reveal brass when the gold thins.
Pro: lighter on the pocket for trend-led designs you may not want to invest gold money into.
Con: the gold layer is thin and wears with friction, sweat and cleaning.
Con: once worn, the silver underneath shows, and that silver can tarnish.
Con: resale value is mostly the silver weight, not the gold.

sections.heading: How long does the plating last?
paragraphs: There is no single honest number, because it depends on plating thickness, where the piece sits on your body and how you treat it. A pendant that hangs against a shirt lasts far longer than a ring that rubs against your phone, keys and steering wheel all day.

Pendants and earrings tend to hold their plating best. Rings, bracelets and toe rings wear fastest. The first places to fade are usually the edges, the bail of a pendant and anywhere that rubs against fabric or skin.

sections.heading: Gold plated silver vs gold plated brass
paragraphs: Both can look identical on day one. The difference appears months later. When gold plating wears off brass, you see a yellowish or reddish base metal that may darken and can leave marks on skin. When it wears off sterling, you see white silver, which looks clean and can be polished.

Brass-based pieces have their place. Varaha's own [Kundan necklace sets](/women/necklaces) are brass with gold plating, which suits festive jewellery worn a few times a year. For a piece you will wear daily, a silver base is the more durable choice.

sections.heading: Five ways to make the gold last longer
paragraphs: Plating wears through friction and chemicals. Reduce both and the finish stays rich for much longer.
list: Spray perfume and apply lotion before you put the piece on, and let it dry.
Remove it for bathing, swimming, workouts and sleeping.
Clean only with lukewarm water, a drop of mild soap and a soft cloth. Skip silver dips, polishing cloths with compound and the foil-and-baking-soda trick.
Store it alone in a soft pouch so other jewellery does not scratch it.
Rotate it with other pieces instead of wearing the same ring every single day.

sections.heading: When the plating fades: your options
paragraphs: Because the base is silver, a faded piece is not finished. Many local jewellers offer re-plating, where they clean the piece and apply a fresh gold layer. Ask whether they can do it without damaging any stones, as some stones need to be removed or protected first.
Some people also like the look of a gold piece that has softened to show a little silver at the edges, and simply keep wearing it. Either way, you still own real silver.

sections.heading: Who gold plated silver suits best
paragraphs: It is a good fit for someone who loves the warmth of gold, wants something for office or college wear, and would rather spend on several designs than one solid gold piece. It also makes a thoughtful gift for people who wear gold tones but do not need an investment piece. You can see gold plated options among Varaha's [925 silver pendants](/silver), where the plating is mentioned on each listing.

faq.a: The gold layer itself does not tarnish easily, but where it wears thin, the silver underneath can darken. Gentle care slows this down.

faq.q: Can gold plated silver be worn daily?
faq.a: Yes, especially pendants and earrings. Remove it for bathing and workouts to keep the plating longer.

faq.q: Can gold plated silver be re-plated?
faq.a: Yes. Many jewellers can clean and re-plate it, though pieces with stones may need extra care during the process.

faq.q: Is gold plated silver better than gold plated brass?
faq.a: For long-term wear, usually yes. When the plating fades, you are left with silver instead of a base metal that can discolour.
